params.script_inline:
import sys, json

# The target of this hive's guarded default door: a request on a lane nobody
# wired comes back as ONE ordinary receipt naming the lane that was asked for,
# on the same lane every occupant answers on.
#
# Not a dead letter. A dead letter is a message the colony lost; this is a
# message the colony read, understood as unaddressed, and answered. An operator
# who mistyped a lane learns which one they typed, in the same round, instead of
# reading a queue.

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
hop = ((doc["envelope"].get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {})
route = str(hop.get("route") or "")
asked = route if route else "(none)"
call_id = str(hop.get("tool_call_id") or "")
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "receipt", "operation": "operator_unknown",
               "error_code": "unknown_route", "route_asked": route,
               "tool_call_id": call_id},
    "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": call_id,
                  "text": "no lane named %s is wired into this hive" % asked}]}))

description.purpose: The target of this hive's guarded default door: a request on a lane nobody wired comes back as ONE ordinary receipt naming the lane that was asked for.
description.use_when: Never wired by hand and never addressed by name. It is reached only when no positive lane door fired, and only because the default door's own guard held.
description.not_in_scope: Not a lane: nothing is read out of the request, nothing is executed and no near-miss name is suggested. And not a drain -- a cell that accepted the request and emitted nothing would be the swallowing sink GH #284 removed from this repository.
description.emits_meaning: route receipt: the one outward lane of this hive, so the caller's single return edge takes this the way it takes every answer. hop.error_code is always `unknown_route` and hop.route_asked is the lane that was asked for, verbatim, including the empty string.
description.consumes_meaning: The request as it arrived. It is not parsed -- what it wanted is irrelevant once there is no lane to serve it.
examples: hop.route == 'in_restart' -> receipt 'no lane named in_restart is wired into this hive', hop { error_code: 'unknown_route', route_asked: 'in_restart' }
a request with no hop.route at all -> the same refusal, route_asked empty -- the caller learns the lane was lost instead of watching the request stall
